info.title: Crumble API
info.description: Shared HTTP contract for Crumble clients. Provider availability and cross-field business rules are validated at runtime.

BearerAuth.description: Better Auth session token from /api/auth/sign-in/email. The legacy server token is not accepted.

VoiceGatewayToken.description: The voice gateway token the owner issues in settings. It reaches only /v1/voice/ routes, which accept nothing else.

SessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
SessionCookie.description: Better Auth session cookie. HTTPS deployments use the __Secure- prefix. Cookie-authenticated writes require the configured Origin.

origin.description: What the bot answered: owner (a message from the owner), task (a scheduled task), script (a script task's result), bot (another bot's request), group (a group chat turn), or coding or desktop (a job's report; jobName names the job). Clients may receive other values later.

jobName.description: The job whose report the bot answered, for origin coding or desktop. A desktop job's report often asks for the owner; clients may open the bot desktop.

groupId.description: Set when a bot answered in a group chat; open the group rather than the bot chat.

waitingFor.description: Set when the bot waits for the owner's answer: approval (a desktop job action held by an intent check, or a call request), credential, or login (a request the owner saves or declines). Clients may receive other values later.

LearnedEvent.description: A bot's review of one of its turns changed its skills or memory, sent as the `learned` event on /v1/events. Clients show a short notice in the bot chat and link to the change record.

displayName.description: The line's display name, or the bot's name.

lines.description: Lines whose bot is enabled; empty while the voice gateway is disabled.

username.description: The line the call is placed from.

to.description: The number to dial: for a call to the owner, the first in the owner's list; for an outside call, the number the owner approved, digits with an optional leading +.

greeting.description: What the bot says when the call is answered: for an outside call, the opening the owner approved, to be spoken verbatim.

party.description: Who is called: owner, or outside, someone other than the owner after the owner approved the bot's call request. Absent means owner. Dial an outside call only when the voice gateway's own config allows it, else report it failed.

VoiceCallEvent.description: A bot asks to call the owner, or someone else after the owner approved it. Sent only to a stream opened with calls=true, and sent again after a reconnect until the call is acknowledged; ignore a callId you already dial.

VoiceCallCancelEvent.description: The call's turn was aborted or its wait ran out: hang up if it still rings.

VoiceGatewayReplacedEvent.description: Another connection with the same voice gateway token took over; sent before this stream closes.

coding.description: Whether bots can be given the coding tool on this server.

desktop.description: Whether bots can be given the desktop tool, and with it a bot desktop, on this server.

jobKinds.description: The kinds of background job bots can be given on this server, such as `coding` and `desktop`.

codingImage.description: Image new workspaces boot from, such as `ghcr.io/owner/image:tag`; null uses the server's `CRUMBLE_WORKSPACE_IMAGE`.

questionGraceMinutes.description: How long a coding job waiting on the owner's answer keeps its workspace running.

reply.description: The bot's reply, read by the message's submission; null unless the execution's status is done. A failed or cancelled execution never gets one.

hangUp.description: True when the bot asked to end the call: hang up once the reply was read aloud, then report the end with reason hungUp.

outcome.description: For a call a bot placed: ringing acknowledges it as soon as dialing starts; the others settle it.
A started call ended. Accepted for an active, ended, or unknown call; an unknown one can't be started afterwards.

reason.description: hungUp: the media ended or the dialog closed. maxDuration: the call reached its maximum length. failed: any other error. stopping: the voice gateway shut down.

login.description: The name commits and pull requests show, such as `scout[bot]`.

account.description: The GitHub user or organization whose repositories the App works on.

user.description: The owner's GitHub login when signed in through the App; its bots then act as the owner, with the App's badge.

passwordManager.description: The password manager the value is read from; null for a value stored in Crumble or no value.

reference.description: Where in `passwordManager` the value is read from.

SecretStatus.description: A secret the owner entered; its value is never returned.

login.description: The GitHub user its bots act and commit as.

signingKey.description: The OpenSSH public key the account's commits are signed with. Add it on GitHub as the user's signing key so its commits show as verified.

judgeModel.description: The owner's classifier; null uses the default, GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI Decisions.

choices.description: The classifier models the account's provider keys reach.

JudgeChoice.description: The model that judges now: a classifier, or a small chat model when no key reaches one. Null when no model is available; then only commit points are held.

visionModel.description: The model that describes images for bots whose model can't read them. Null when off: such bots refuse images in their chat and get only an image's name in group chats.

choices.description: The chat models that read images and that the account's provider keys reach.

BotAvatarDefinition.description: Open Bot Avatar v1 geometry in a 0 0 100 100 viewBox, body color and eye color.

tools.description: The bot's tools; always includes `schedule` and `codemode`.

sharedMemory.description: True whenever `tools` includes `memory`; the server ignores it in input.

delegates.description: Every other bot; with `delegate` in `tools` this bot may message any of them. The server ignores it in input.

desktopModel.description: The model for this bot's desktop jobs; unset, they use the bot's own model.

review.description: How the bot reviews its turns to learn: whether at all, after how many tool-activity rounds for skills and memory, and how much of a turn a review reads. Unset means enabled with thresholds of 10.

reviewModel.description: The model that runs this bot's reviews; unset, they use the bot's own model.

live.description: Pi Durable live progress state. In-flight assistant message content is omitted.

partial.description: Text of the reply the bot is writing now. Empty unless the event stream was opened with partial=true.

kind.description: The entry's kind. Events include bot-message, job-question, held-action, job-failure, reset, compaction, call-started (content: the greeting of a call the bot placed, or Call started), and call-ended (content: how the call ended, when it woke no bot turn). Clients may receive other values later.

jobQuestion.description: On a `job-question` event: the job that asked the owner the question in `content`. Whether it still waits is the job's `question` in its listing.

heldAction.description: On a `held-action` event: the desktop job action waiting for the owner. Its state is under `/v1/agents/{id}/held-actions`.

direction.description: outbound: the bot called the owner, or the callee of an outside call.

callee.description: Set on an outside call, which the bot placed to someone other than the owner: who it called. A call-started event then reads as the bot calling the callee, its content the opening.

call.description: On a `call-started` or `call-ended` event: the call.

toolDetails.description: Provider-specific tool details, including nested code-mode calls. A successful `desktop_screenshot` result has `{ mimeType, size }`; read its image from `GET /v1/agents/{id}/attachments/{entryId}/0`.

sources.description: In a group chat, the pages the sending bot searched or read in the turn that wrote the message.

kind.description: Where the message came from: owner, task, event (an event automation's prompt), script (a script task's result), credential, bot, group, call (a voice gateway call ended, which starts a bot turn), call_request (the owner declined a call request), or callee (what the callee of an outside call said, in that call's conversation only). Clients may receive other values later.

via.description: On an owner message sent through a message gateway: the gateway's ID, such as `discord`. On a spoken message from a voice gateway call: `voice`.

source.description: On an event automation's message: the name of the event source whose event started it.

model.description: The model the job runs with. Absent when the job has none of its own and uses the server's default.

usage.description: Pi Durable usage document of the job's own conversation: tokens and cost per model and tool. Absent before its first request.

options.description: Answers the owner can pick; any other text is an answer too.

multiple.description: Whether several options can be picked; the answer lists each.

question.description: The question the job asked the owner and waits on. Answer it with the job's `answer` route.

model.description: The model the job runs with. Absent when the job has none of its own and uses the server's default.

usage.description: Pi Durable usage document of the job's own conversation: tokens and cost per model and tool. Absent before its first request.

options.description: Answers the owner can pick; any other text is an answer too.

multiple.description: Whether several options can be picked; the answer lists each.

question.description: The question the job asked the owner and waits on. Answer it with the job's `answer` route.

holder.description: Who operates the bot desktop. While the owner holds control, the bot's desktop job pauses and only the owner's viewer input reaches the bot desktop.

changes.description: How often control changed hands. A desktop job refuses actions it planned before a change.

running.description: Whether the bot's machine runs its bot desktop now, so a passive viewer can connect. Always false for a bot without a bot desktop.

path.description: Server-relative URL of the viewer page, a noVNC client of the bot desktop. Load it in a web view; it works once and expires at expiresAt unless its connection has started by then.

memberIds.description: Member bots in the order they joined.

paused.description: Bot-started turns used up the turn budget; the owner's next message resumes the group.

botTurns.description: Bot-started turns since the owner's last message.

error.description: Why the member's latest turn failed.

lastError.description: Why the newest use couldn't read the value from its password manager; null when it could.

github.description: The value is a GitHub token: from the bot's GitHub App, minted for the App or for the owner signed in through it, or its machine account's personal access token. It has no secret here.

instructions.default: You are a thoughtful, capable personal assistant.

number.description: The number to dial, normalized: digits with an optional leading +.

opening.description: What the bot says first when the callee answers.

status.description: pending: waiting for the owner. calling: approved, and the call rings or runs. ended: see outcome.

outcome.description: Set once the status is ended.

error.description: Why the value couldn't be read from its password manager; the request was never sent.

fields.description: Where each field's value is read from. A login always has a username and a password; `one_time_code` only when it has one.

lastError.description: Why the newest fill couldn't read its value; null when it could.

oneTimeCode.description: Whether the bot says the site asks for a one-time code.

error.description: Why the value couldn't be read; nothing was typed.

page.description: The URL of the page the job read last.

ownerMessages.description: The owner messages the action was checked against.

reason.description: Why the intent check held it.

name.description: The task, bot, or group chat, as named when the memory was saved.

MemorySource.description: Where the memory was saved: the owner's bot chat, the owner directly, a scheduled task, another bot's request, or a group chat.

path.description: The skill's folder; empty for the root.

digest.description: Fingerprint of the imported files; an update is available when upstream's differs.

SkillOrigin.description: Where an installed skill came from. Installed skills are read-only.

removed.description: The skill's folder is gone from the branch.

SkillUpdate.description: The newer upstream commit of an installed skill.

omitted.description: Skills beyond the first hundred, not listed.

path.description: The skill's folder; empty for the root.

problem.description: Why a `clash` or `invalid` skill can't be installed.

skipped.description: Files in the folder that won't be imported: only SKILL.md and references/*.md are.

eventSourceId.description: The event source whose events start this automation; set instead of `cron` and `runAt`.

output.description: The last 64 KiB and 2000 lines of combined output.

droppedBytes.description: Bytes dropped from the output tail.

thinkingLevels.description: The thinking levels this model takes, from lowest to highest. A bot's level outside them runs at the nearest one.

usedBy.description: The keys of the secrets that read their value from this password manager, such as `mcp:<server ID>`; it can't be disconnected while any remain.

contributes.description: What the plugin adds to the server, so a client can show its settings where those are chosen.

kind.description: A secret is written once and never returned.

whenMissing.description: The status to show while the setting has no value.

error.description: Why the server's tools were left out of a bot's last turn, such as a missing sign-in; null once it connects again.

oauthClientId.description: The client ID of an OAuth app the owner registered with the server's authorization server, used instead of registering Crumble.

get.description: Server-sent events for the voice gateway. A config event comes first and after every change to lines, owner numbers, or their bots. With calls=true, call and cancel events ask the gateway to place and hang up calls to the owner. One stream is live per account: a new connection sends replaced to the older one and closes it. Revoking or replacing the token closes the stream.

schema.description: With calls=true, the voice gateway declares it can place calls: bots with a line that may call the owner are offered the call_owner tool, approved call requests can dial, and call events arrive on this stream.

parameters.description: With calls=true, the voice gateway declares it can place calls: bots with a line that may call the owner are offered the call_owner tool, approved call requests can dial, and call events arrive on this stream.
parameters.name: calls

200.description: SSE stream, not a JSON array

401.description: Missing, revoked, or replaced voice gateway token

post.description: Sends what the owner said on a call to the line's bot. On the line's active outside call, what the callee said goes to that call's conversation instead, never the bot chat, under requestId outside-call:{callId}:{requestId}. The same IDs with other content answer 409, and so do a callId whose call ended and an outside call's ID that is not the line's active call: hang up. A callId the server doesn't know is accepted.

put.description: Reports that a call on the line started, before the greeting is spoken; send it again after every config event while the call runs. For a call a bot placed, it also settles the call as answered. A call nobody confirms within 15 seconds of a new events stream, or 60 seconds without one, ends. 409 when the call ended, another call is active on the line, or the callId is an outside call's that no longer rings: hang up.
